documentation.range: This species is found off the coast of southern Australia from eastern Victoria to south-western Australia, including Tasmania (Jereb et al. 2014). Type locality: “Australia”
documentation.population: There is no population information available for this species.
documentation.habitats: This shallow intertidal (0-50 m) species inhabits a wide variety of areas including reefs, seagrass beds and rubble areas. It forages nocturnally for crustaceans and fishes. Eggs are carried within a web and develop into benthic hatchlings. Tetrodotoxin, which is extremely venomous, is produced in the salivary glands detected in the eggs, arms, abdomen and 'cephalothorax' of this species. This venom can be deadly to humans (Jereb et al. 2014).
documentation.threats: This species may be affected by global warming and the greenhouse effect as it occurs on coral reefs which are sensitive to ocean acidification.
documentation.measures: There are no conservation measures in place for this species. We recommend that further research is conducted to determine the population status and ecology of this species. Research is also required to determine whether this species is affected by any significant threats, such as harvesting.
documentation.use_trade: There is no use or trade information for this species.
documentation.rationale: Hapalochlaena maculosa is assessed as Least Concern because it has a large geographic distribution. Nonetheless we recommend that further research is conducted to determine the population status and ecology of this species. Research is also required to determine whether this species is affected by any significant threats.
